title: How do we give eight pairs of fractions the same fractional unit?
description: Eight pairs of fractions are each rewritten as equivalent fractions with the same bottom number. The board finds a number that both bottom numbers go into, and multiplies the top and the bottom of each fraction to reach it. The last step checks that the bottom numbers match.
teaching_notes: One idea: find a number that both bottom numbers go into, then multiply the top and the bottom of each fraction by what is needed to reach it. Watch for students who change only the bottom number.

source: In-text exercise, pairs with the same fractional units (section 7.6)
video_script.why: A learner rewrites pairs of fractions with the same fractional unit by the method of the solved example: reach a common bottom number by multiplying the top and the bottom.
video_script.substitution: the book's own eight pairs of fractions
video_script.anchor: eight pairs of fractions written on the board
video_script.payoff_line: every pair now has one fractional unit

final_answer.spoken: every pair now has one fractional unit, with the common bottom numbers ten, six, twenty, thirty-five, four, ninety, twelve and eighteen

video_script.fraction_reading: seven halves, three fifths, eight thirds, five sixths, three fourths, six sevenths, eight fifths, nine fourths, five halves, one tenth, two ninths, eleven fourths, thirteen sixths, one ninth
never_show: a pair whose bottom numbers still differ in the answer
maths_rules: 3 goes into 6: 8/3 = (8 x 2)/(3 x 2) = 16/6 and 5/6 stays 5/6
video_script.design: Eight pairs stay on the board. Each pair gets one bottom number that both fractions can reach, by the method of the solved example. The worklist uses the smallest such number, so one bottom number is kept when it already goes into the other.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; eight pairs of fractions written in two columns: 7/2 and 3/5, 8/3 and 5/6, 3/4 and 3/5, 6/7 and 8/5, 9/4 and 5/2, 1/10 and 2/9, 8/3 and 11/4, 13/6 and 1/9

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.pairs: eight pairs of fractions appear in two columns, each pair with different bottom numbers circled
marks.ask: the words same fractional unit appear above the pairs

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, and it has eight pairs of fractions.
<bookmark mark='pairs'/>In each pair, the two bottom numbers are different.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How do we write each pair with the same fractional unit?

beats.on_screen: the eight pairs hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 3/5 = (3 x 2)/(5 x 2) = 6/10 with the multiplier 2 circled; a note says same amount, new fractional unit; two fractions with the same bottom number are boxed together

marks.rule: 3/5 changes to (3 x 2)/(5 x 2) = 6/10 with the multiplier circled
marks.goal: two fractions with the same bottom number are boxed together with the note one fractional unit

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Multiplying the top and the bottom by the same number gives an equivalent fraction.
<bookmark mark='goal'/>We want both fractions of a pair to have the same bottom number. Then they use one fractional unit.

beats.on_screen: Given: 8 pairs of fractions with different bottom numbers
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, there are eight pairs of fractions, and each pair has different bottom numbers.

beats.on_screen: To find: equivalent fractions for each pair with the same fractional unit
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each pair as equivalent fractions with the same fractional unit.

marks.way: the words find a number that both bottom numbers go into are written
marks.ten: 7/2 and 3/5 are written and 10 is circled

beats.colours: the common bottom number = accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='way'/>Step one, we use the same way as the solved example in your book. Find a number that both bottom numbers go into.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Take seven halves and three fifths. The numbers two and five both go into ten.
<bookmark mark='mul'/>Seven times five over two times five is thirty-five tenths. Three times two over five times two is six tenths.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: one bottom number goes into the other. 8/3 and 5/6: use 6; 8/3 = 16/6 and 5/6 stays. 9/4 and 5/2: use 4; 5/2 = 10/4 and 9/4 stays

marks.six: 8/3 and 5/6 are written and 6 is circled
marks.keep: 8/3 changes to 16/6 and 5/6 stays the same
marks.four: 9/4 and 5/2 are written, 4 is circled, 5/2 changes to 10/4 and 9/4 stays the same

beats.colours: the common bottom number = accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='six'/>Step two, sometimes one bottom number goes into the other. Take eight thirds and five sixths. Three goes into six, so use six.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>Eight thirds becomes sixteen sixths, and five sixths stays the same.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Take nine fourths and five halves. Two goes into four, so use four. Five halves becomes ten fourths, and nine fourths stays.

beats.colours: the common bottom number = accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='twenty'/>Step three, three fourths and three fifths use twenty. They become fifteen twentieths and twelve twentieths.
<bookmark mark='thirtyfive'/>Six sevenths and eight fifths use thirty-five. They become thirty thirty-fifths and fifty-six thirty-fifths.
<bookmark mark='ninety'/>One tenth and two ninths use ninety. They become nine ninetieths and twenty ninetieths.
<bookmark mark='twelve'/>Eight thirds and eleven fourths use twelve. They become thirty-two twelfths and thirty-three twelfths.

marks.nine: 13/6 and 1/9 are written and the multiples 9, 18 are listed
marks.eighteen: 18 is circled and the pair changes to 39/18 and 2/18

beats.colours: the common bottom number = accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='nine'/>Step four, take thirteen sixths and one ninth. Count in the bigger bottom number: nine, eighteen.
<bookmark mark='eighteen'/>Six goes into eighteen, so use eighteen. Thirteen sixths becomes thirty-nine eighteenths, and one ninth becomes two eighteenths.

beats.on_screen: Check: every pair now has equal bottom numbers; 39/18 divided top and bottom by 3 gives 13/6

marks.same: the eight finished pairs are lined up and the bottom numbers are ticked
marks.back: 39/18 is divided top and bottom by 3 and 13/6 comes back

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step five, check each pair. The two bottom numbers now match in every one of the eight pairs.
<bookmark mark='back'/>Also, divide thirty-nine and eighteen by three, and we get back thirteen sixths.

marks.ans: the eight finished pairs are boxed
marks.bottoms: the eight common bottom numbers are circled

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Every pair now has one fractional unit, so the fractions in it can be compared.
<bookmark mark='bottoms'/>The common bottom numbers are ten, six, twenty, thirty-five, four, ninety, twelve and eighteen.
